direction_en:
Time: A bright Sunday afternoon
Location: A tatami room facing the garden
Leaning back in a rattan chair on the porch, reading the newspaper.
text_en: "The manager Turner from the American Fuller Building Materials Company visited Mejiro Cultural Village and remarked, 'Ah, it's a miniature Los Angeles!' Today, Mejiro Cultural Village has become a charming and beautiful residential area."

direction_en: Sitting near the porch, spreading a cushion and knitting.
text_en: What’s that supposed to mean?

"In the 40,000 tsubo area, there are orderly roads, sanitary sewage systems, electric heating, tennis courts, and many neat bungalows and grand light-style buildings, as well as elegant villa-style Japanese architecture, all wrapped in the cheerful environment of a highland rich in views of Mount Fuji and trees..." (throws the newspaper aside) Hey, how about a walk?
Why don’t you just go visit Kawakami-san?
I really don’t have to go.
I prefer to act on a whim, you know.
A walk, huh?
A walk or whatever else...
Well, if it’s just a walk or whatever, is there anything else you want to do?
No, and that’s perfectly fine.
Ah.
Why don’t you just go visit Kawakami-san? Stop saying such things.
I really don’t want to go anymore.
Just go, will you?
I’m not going. I want to stay by your side. You really don’t get it, do you?
Oh, I understand perfectly well, your highness.
Ah, so this is what a rare Sunday feels like.
Absolutely.

direction_en: He picks up the newspaper again, reading it absentmindedly.
text_en: You know, it would be amusing to hold a contest in the newspaper about how to handle situations like this.
I’ll enter it.

direction_en: Still engrossed in the newspaper, he feigns disinterest.
text_en: What would you submit?
What would the question be?
The question? Well, it would be about how to spend a Sunday after one year of marriage.
I wouldn’t know how to answer that.
It’s not that complicated. Come on, you tell me.
A method for keeping the wife from getting bored on Sunday.
And a way that doesn’t annoy the husband...
That sounds fine.
Do you have a brilliant idea?
I do. First, the woman should get up in the morning, head straight to the hot water, do her makeup properly, change into a nice kimono, and say she’s going to visit a friend.
And then...?
Then the man will surely make a face of displeasure.
Not necessarily.
I’m talking about you.
When have I ever made a face like that?
You don’t.
Well, fine. What happens next?

You'll make a face, won't you? Well, here's the thing—I'm not really keen on going, but if it turns out later that I've just been lounging around at home, that would be awkward... So, every time we meet, they say, 'Come visit us! On Sundays, my husband will be around, and we can go see a play together.' Today, since you're here with me anyway, I thought I might just pop over. Or, if you have other plans, I could gently ask you about that.
Gently, huh? Well, I don't mind either way, but what about lunch? What will you do without me?
I've already prepared some tea and snacks for lunch.
What about dinner?
For dinner, I thought I’d stop by 'Azumaya' on my way out and get some 'Oyako' (parent-child dish).
Oyako again? You’ll be late coming back.
True, I can't say for sure, but if it hits ten o'clock, please lay out the bedding and go to sleep.

Do you have any money on you? 
Well, I'm completely out.
Then here, take this. Here’s ten yen.
Thank you.
The night air is getting chilly, so take a scarf with you.
Alright.
Now, I think I'll take my time and read a book. Please make sure the bath is ready. If guests arrive, we still have some leftover biscuits... I won't bother shaving today. Ah, what a peaceful Sunday.
What’s wrong?
You’re hopeless.
Why's that?
Just because.
Oh, I see. If you were a man, what would you do in a situation like this?
In a situation like this...?
Should I stop?
You should stop, or at least say something.
What should I say to stop?
If we can avoid going, then today, why not spend some time together, or something like that...?
I see. What if I say I want to spend time together?
Then go ahead.
Sure, go if you want. But what if you don’t want to? What if you do want to, but circumstances don’t allow it? Like today.
Well then, it’s fine if the play becomes an activity.
An activity...? That’s not something couples should go see together.
Why not?
Just ask anyone.
That’s the problem with you. I’m not like other women.
You probably are. And that’s exactly why it’s more dangerous.
What are you talking about?
It seems like it’s better not to go out after all.
Well then, just go ahead, visit Kawakami or whoever.

You’re being persistent. What did you say this morning? When I said I was going to Kawakami’s, you said, 'Why would you be so infatuated with someone you see every day at the office? You wouldn’t lose anything by staying home for a day on the weekend.' That’s what you said.
So what?
It doesn’t matter. The real question is why you’re doing this.
Oh, is it wrong to be like this?
Here we are, and yet, there’s a way to be here, isn’t there? I read the newspaper. You start knitting. I sigh. You sigh too. I yawn. You yawn as well. I…
So when I suggest we go somewhere, you come up with all sorts of excuses…
Alright, I get that. But we didn’t get married just to go somewhere on Sundays. We should be able to have a bit more cheer in our lives at home.
That’s because you don’t talk.
Talk… what is there to talk about?
Talking is something you ‘do.’ It’s not just something that ‘exists.’
What’s that… Philosophy? Fine, let’s say talking is something you ‘do.’ But you don’t talk either.
You say that because I’m noisy.
That’s because you chatter away while I’m doing something.
That’s not true, I can talk even after we go to bed.
I’m too sleepy for that.
To be honest, I’m perfectly happy just being quietly by your side. If only you paid a little more attention to me, it would be wonderful…
What’s for dinner?
Not decided yet, it depends on how today goes.
You’re still like a schoolgirl.

What do you mean by that? I always think that on Sundays, when we have the time, we could go see a play or eat something delicious. Those things are nice, but there are also plenty of more homely pleasures to enjoy. Even the garden could be better. If you helped out, we could easily create a little flower bed. Just look at all the cosmos blooming right now. They’re beautiful from outside too.
That’s why you’re like a schoolgirl.
Then you’re like an elementary school student.
Is there really such a thing?
There is!
Hey, let’s go for a walk.
It’s too late for that.
Anywhere nearby will do.
Where, Inokashira?
Tama River would be fine.
Then we should take our time and plan for lunch somewhere. Otherwise, it’ll be boring.
How much do you have on hand?
I’m done with that talk for today.
Sixteen, seventeen, eighteen, nineteen….
Well, we should have prepared since morning and left right after breakfast.
Let’s decide the night before.
Right, so where are we going?
A day trip to Kamakura sounds nice.
I have a place I want to go.
If we do that, there’s a train leaving Tokyo Station at eight-something.
Second class.
Of course. We need to grab those seats facing the window quickly. I’ll put my stick and your parasol right here on the net….
I’d prefer to hold it.
Oh, I see. The ones coming in after us will look at us and think, 'Ah, they’re having fun,' and try to sit as close as possible.
You’re such a fool.
The train starts moving.
Could you open the window, please?
You'll let in the soot. Look over there, that's the site of Hamarikyu.
Oh, really.
Shinagawa, Shinagawa, transfer to the Yamanote Line.
That was quick. I'm going to buy some caramel.
Alright, hey, caramel.
What about you?
I'll take some. We're passing Omori now, and soon you'll see the president's house.
That's the stingy house, right?
A stingy house indeed. Skipping Kamata and Kawasaki, heading straight to Yokohama. No need to stop here. Next up, Hodogaya, Totsuka, and now we're coming to Ofuna.
I'm going to buy a sandwich.
Alright, hey, sandwich.
What about you?
Hmm, I'll take some.
No way, you can eat it all by yourself.
Alright, I'm ready to get off. Let me put on my geta...
I'm not just going to sit here, come on...
First, we'll head to Hachiman Shrine, I suppose. Do you know it?
I know it well. But first, let's go see the coast.
Well, that sounds fine. Let me see...
We can just call a car.
Right, a taxi it is. You go ahead and get in first.
Excuse me, then.
Now, let me light my cigarette.
But first, you should tell the driver where we're headed.
How about the beach?
That's a bit odd, just to the beach. Excuse me, driver, take us to the seaside hotel.
Isn't the seaside hotel closed?
You're joking.
Well, there's nothing we can do. Let's go. Beep, beep, beep...
What’s that? It’s already here.
Good grief. Well then, please take us to a room with a nice view.
The dining room will do just fine.
Right, so you order something.
What about you?
I’m fine with anything.
Then, two cold Calpis, please.
Hey, you, there's still some time before noon, so I think I'll take a little walk around. I'll be back by twelve, so make sure to have something delicious ready for me.
Alright.
I'd like to stay here for a while. Do you have any nice rooms available? One with a bathroom...?
A bathroom, you mean... a bath?
Right. Oh, yes. Let's go with that. No need to see it first. By the way, don’t you have a plane at your place?
You.
No? Well, that can’t be helped. We'll walk then. Now, where's my suitcase...?
You haven't forgotten it on the train again, have you?
No, I gave it to the bellboy. Ah, there it is.
Where are we headed?
That over there is Enoshima.
What a lovely view.
Be careful, or you might trip. Here, let me take your hand.
People will see us.
Let them see. They’ll be the ones missing out. Are you tired? Well then, let’s take a break here. If you want, we can go to the sea anytime.
I’m going in.
Go ahead. Hmm, you have quite a nice figure when you're undressed. Just don’t wander too far.
I’ll be fine.

Wait, wait! Stay right there. Let me take a picture. Okay, smile! Hmm, this is wonderful. (growing more excited) I've never seen you look so beautiful before. How about that shape... what a stunning color! Oh, by the way, your hair is that long? And your chest is that full? Ah, you're laughing. Turn this way and let me see. Yes, those are your eyes. Oh, that mouth... (shouting as if forgetting himself)!
You.
Come here and take a look.
Come and see.
No.
Come on, just take a look.

direction_en: (stands up, takes her husband’s hands, and shakes them)
text_en: You really have no idea how to express yourself, do you?
How about this?
No, don’t do that.
Do you really not get tired of me? Of us like this...?
What about you?
Honestly, being with you is becoming less enjoyable for me. That’s true. But when I think about what it would be like without you, I feel like I can’t sit still or stand still. That’s true too.
Which part is true?

Both are true. (pause) That’s why I think this can’t go on. But I feel helpless. (pause) You’re just sitting there, quietly knitting by my side. Are you really satisfied with that? There’s no way you are. I can imagine you sitting alone in some corner of the room, lost in thought while I’m out. I picture your lonely face so many times while I’m outside. Don’t you get tired of our life, where we’re only interested in how to spend less than a hundred yen every month? You might have resigned yourself to it by now, thinking there’s no point in complaining. But you’re not a woman without ideals. I want to know what you’re thinking these days. What will happen to us if we keep living like this? Am I wrong? Or are you just replaying the dreams you had as a girl?
You’re such a fool. (tries to laugh but ends up looking teary)
Everyone’s a fool. We don’t even understand ourselves. Let’s stop this talk.
But it’s been a while since I cried.
It’s only natural for you to feel dissatisfied when I go out on Sundays without you. You must want a break sometimes. It’s nothing serious. How about we have dinner and then go out?
Let’s go then. Hurry up and take a bath.
Not today.
Why not?
It's already the third day for you.
Yes, I'm feeling a bit under the weather... but I'll be fine today. More importantly, it's three-thirty now, so... I'll step out for a bit before dinner.

direction_en: She returns to her seat, looking somewhat resentful.
text_en: Where do you think you're going?
Oh, I'll be back soon.

direction_en: She stares at him, about to say something, then suddenly looks down.
text_en: Well, fine.
It’s not to Kawakami’s place.
Anywhere is fine, really.
You think I'm going to play billiards, don't you?
Go ahead, just leave.
Are you angry?
What’s wrong with you?
It’s my fault.
It’s not about right or wrong. That's why I'm going out later.
I understand now.
What do you understand?
I’m just going to give up already.
Give up on what...?
I'm sorry.
This is strange.
It's quite amusing, isn't it? Other wives seem to revel in the freedom when their husbands are out. But I've always found that strange.
Well, it's only natural to find that strange.
But today, it's finally stopped being strange to me.
Oh?
Men really are made to leave in the morning and come back at night.
Why do men act like being at home is such a favor? Women can't stand it.
It's not like I'm doing you a favor.
So if you have somewhere to go, just go quickly. I'd feel much better that way.

direction_en: sits back down and starts reading the newspaper

text_en: I dread Sundays.
So do I.
You spoil me too much, you know. (starts knitting)
I don't think that's true.
Yes, it is.
It's a complicated matter.
Just look at other households.
I am looking.
You should be more like them.
I can't do it.
Women tend to get carried away.
I know that.
Well, that's fine then.
I think we're doing pretty well, all things considered.
Just a little more effort, that's all.
Is it money?
That's not it.
Should we get a dog?
Wouldn't a little bird be better?
Hey, shall we talk about something?
Sure.

Once upon a time, there was a man and a woman. The man started working right after graduating from school. The woman was still attending girls' school. Every morning, they met at the same time at the same station in the suburbs. Eventually, they began to bow to each other. If the man arrived early, he would wait for the woman. If the woman arrived early, she would...
...go on ahead.
That sort of thing happened.

direction_en: At this moment, a girl's voice cries out, 'Oh!' A large paper balloon rolls into the garden.
He tosses aside the newspaper and goes down to the garden to pick up the balloon.

text_en: Is Chieko-chan at home today?

direction_en: He silently begins to bat at the balloon.

text_en: Oh, stop that, dear... (calling out loudly) Chieko-chan, come here! Let’s play with the balloon together!

direction_en: He continues to enthusiastically bat at the balloon.
She stands up, goes to get her sandals from the entrance, and descends into the garden.
text_en: You can’t hit it so hard, dear... (as if addressing a child who seems to be on the other side of the fence) Now, let’s play with the balloon together. (Saying this, she playfully snatches the balloon from him) Chieko-chan, come around from that side!

direction_en: Following her, looking a bit frustrated.
text_en: Hey, let me have a turn, will you...?
